questions.q: Why is checking for duplicate invoices a common, important task for an AP consultant?
options: Paying the same invoice twice is a common and costly mistake, so catching duplicates before payment matters
It has no real business impact
Duplicate invoices are always intentional fraud and nothing else
Oracle Fusion automatically prevents all duplicate invoices with no consultant involvement needed
questions.explain: Duplicate invoice payments are one of the most common and expensive AP errors, which is why this check is built so often.

questions.q: Why group by both vendor_id AND invoice_num, rather than invoice_num alone, when checking for duplicate invoices?
options: Grouping by invoice_num alone would be exactly as accurate
Two different suppliers can legitimately use the same invoice number, so grouping by both avoids false positives
Oracle requires at least two columns in every GROUP BY
vendor_id must always be the first column listed in GROUP BY
questions.explain: The same invoice_num from two unrelated suppliers is a coincidence, not a duplicate — grouping by both columns correctly identifies true duplicates.

questions.q: What does `GROUP BY vendor_id, invoice_num HAVING COUNT(*) > 1` return?
options: The full row details of every duplicate invoice
Every invoice in the table, regardless of duplication
A summary: which vendor_id/invoice_num combinations repeat, and how many times
Only invoices with zero occurrences
questions.explain: This GROUP BY/HAVING pattern returns a summary count per combination, not the individual row details.

questions.q: In the ROW_NUMBER() approach, what does filtering to `WHERE rn > 1` return?
options: Only the first occurrence of each duplicate invoice
Every row in the table
A single summary row per supplier
The actual duplicate rows beyond the first occurrence, with all columns intact
questions.explain: ROW_NUMBER() assigns 1 to the first occurrence within each partition; filtering to rn > 1 isolates the extra duplicate rows themselves.

questions.q: When would you prefer the GROUP BY/HAVING approach over ROW_NUMBER() for duplicate checking?
options: Never — ROW_NUMBER() is always strictly better
When you want a quick summary of how many duplicates exist and for which keys, before investigating the detail rows
GROUP BY cannot be used for duplicate checking at all
When you need the full row details of each duplicate
questions.explain: GROUP BY/HAVING is well suited to a quick summary (which keys repeat, how often), while ROW_NUMBER() is better for retrieving the actual duplicate row details.
